paragraphs: Can/Am Technologies sells Teller, a cashiering and point-of-sale package made for local and state government agencies across North America. More than 80 state and local governments use it for cashiering, payment technology, and credit processing. The idea is a single hub that centralizes revenue collection, credit processing, and reconciliation.

Residents pay through web and mobile portals, which clear through a processor cloud. Departments that collect revenue submit structured batches directly instead of handing paper to a cashier to re-key. Lockbox files, third-party systems, and online application payments import automatically on a schedule the agency sets. At the close of business Teller posts a single organized general ledger entry while accounts receivable stays in sync. It also produces the ICL file carrying scanned check images and MICR data so checks clear electronically.

The stated audience is state and local governments, education, and utilities. The company cites over 20 years of experience in those markets. Teller integrates with financials, accounts receivable, tax, parking, and records systems. Every modification to a payment, session, or batch is recorded and shown as an audit timeline.
